Days after shipping the largest open model ever built, Moonshot paused new subscriptions. Not a billing glitch, a GPU crunch, it could not keep up with demand for its own model. Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters, and if the lab that trained it, sitting on a data center, is scrambling for the compute to serve it, the advice to self-host it that filled your feed last week is worth a second look.
At 4-bit, K3’s weights come to about 1.4 TB. Your GPU has 24 GB. You are not running this on anything you own, and neither is almost anyone else.
Why You Reached for Your GPU
The internet reacted to the Kimi K3 announcement exactly how you would expect. Developers saw the open weights label and started calculating how to fit the model on their home servers. The appeal makes sense. An open model that competes head-to-head with the best proprietary models feels like a victory for the engineering community.
When a company releases a highly capable model for free, the instinct is to figure out how to pull it down and spin it up locally. We did…
